review.translation: [Behold|0], [today|3] [you have driven|1] [me|2] [out|1] [from|4] [the surface of|5] [the ground|6], [and|7] [I will be hidden|8] [from your presence|7]. [And I will be|9] [a fugitive|10] [and a wanderer|11] [on the earth|12], [and it will happen|13] {that} [anyone|14] [who finds me|15] [will kill me|16]!”

analysis.evidence: Cain opens with הֵן to draw attention to what God has done. גֵּרַשְׁתָּ אֹתִי הַיּוֹם means “you have driven me out today,” and Cain goes on to describe the consequences.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected presentative particle without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: look, see (a fact put before the hearer)

analysis.evidence: Cain addresses God. אֹתִי (“me”) identifies Cain as the one driven out, and מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (“from the face of the ground”) specifies where he is driven from.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, second person masculine singular, with the ending ־תָּ

draft.change: Add Genesis 4:14 to the evidence for the existing object-pronoun sense in et.
draft.definition: With a pronominal suffix, אֵת expresses the direct object separately from the verb.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:14 gives a first-person singular example. In גֵּרַשְׁתָּ אֹתִי, Cain is the object of “you have driven away.”

analysis.evidence: Cain says גֵּרַשְׁתָּ אֹתִי, “you have driven me away.” The verb identifies the addressee as the one acting, and אֹתִי identifies the speaker as the one driven away.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle in the suffixed form אֹת־ with the first-person common singular pronominal suffix ־ִי.
analysis.sense: Carries a pronominal suffix as the direct object of a verb.

analysis.evidence: In גֵּרַשְׁתָּ אֹתִי הַיּוֹם, “you have driven me out today,” הַיּוֹם places Cain’s expulsion on the day he is speaking.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + common noun, masculine singular absolute, used adverbially.

analysis.evidence: In גֵּרַשְׁתָּ אֹתִי הַיּוֹם מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, Cain says, ‘You have driven me today from the face of the ground.’ עַל places him on the ground’s surface, and מֵ־ marks his removal from it.
פְּנֵי is in construct with הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground.” Cain says he has been driven מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the surface of the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, plural construct.

analysis.evidence: Cain says he has been driven מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “from the face of the ground.” The construct פְּנֵי supplies “face,” and הָאֲדָמָה names the ground whose surface he must leave.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: Cain addresses God directly. In וּמִפָּנֶיךָ אֶסָּתֵר ‘and from your presence I shall be hidden’, the suffixed preposition identifies whose presence Cain will be hidden from.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + מִן ‘from’ with its נ assimilated to פ + פָּנִים in the plural construct with a second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ ‘your’.

analysis.evidence: וּמִפָּנֶיךָ means “and from your face.” Cain says that, as a consequence of being driven away, he will be hidden from God’s sight.
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, first person common singular, with no attached particle or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Cain describes the consequence of his expulsion. The participles נָע וָנָד express his future condition, giving the clause the sense “and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal weqatal, first person common singular, with prefixed conjunction וְ־ and perfect ending ־תִי
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: Cain says he has been driven from the ground. In וְהָיִיתִי נָע וָנָד בָּאָרֶץ, נָע pairs with וָנָד to describe how he will wander through the land.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with וְהָיִיתִי.
analysis.sense: to wander from place to place

analysis.evidence: Cain says he has been driven from the ground. After וְהָיִיתִי ‘I will be’, נָד is paired with נָע to describe Cain wandering about the earth (בָּאָרֶץ), echoing the sentence pronounced in Genesis 4:12.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וָ־ prefixed to נָד, Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: Cain says he will be נָע וָנָד, “a fugitive and a wanderer.” בָּאָרֶץ names the wider world in which he will wander after being driven from הָאֲדָמָה, the ground he worked.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, followed by a common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: Cain anticipates the consequence of his wandering. וְהָיָה introduces the whole clause כָל־מֹצְאִי יַהַרְגֵנִי, “whoever finds me will kill me.”
analysis.morphology: Qal weqatal (perfect with prefixed וְ), third person masculine singular, used impersonally with future reference.

analysis.evidence: כָל quantifies the singular participle מֹצְאִי, “one who finds me.” Cain fears that anyone who finds him will kill him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָל מֹצְאִי יַהַרְגֵנִי, “whoever finds me will kill me,” the participle identifies the person who finds Cain. Its suffix ־ִי refers to Cain as the one found.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, with a first-person singular object suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָל מֹצְאִי means “whoever finds me” and supplies the singular subject. The suffix ־נִי refers to Cain, who fears that whoever finds him will kill him.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, with a first person common singular object suffix.
